TOURISM 
 
Laois Destination and Experience Development Plan (DEDP) 
The Laois Destination and Experience Development Plan (DEDP) is a five-year sustainable 
tourism development plan being developed by Fáilte Ireland in partnership with Laois County 
Council. The purpose of this plan is to provide a clear and coordinated approach for the 
development of tourism across the county and to maximise the potential of the tourism industry 
over the next five years. Projects and destination development activities are organised into 
a five-year action plan.  
 
The key objectives of the Laois DEDP are to motivate visitors to visit, stay and spend, extend 
the season and disperse visitors across the county through a sustainable tourism development 
approach.    
 
Consultation has now commenced on the Plan with responses are due by Friday, 13th February 
through the following link https://repuconconsulting.welcomesyourfeedback.net/s/LaoisDEDP

Active Travel 
Active Travel Programme 2026 
Laois County Council will continue to receive Active Travel funding from the National 
Transport Authority for 2026. The approved allocation in the sum of €3.5 million has 
been announced and further details will be provided in due course.  Whilst the Council 
awaits the NTA’s funding announcement, there are schemes which are continuing from 
2025. 
 
Mountmellick Permeability Scheme 
Works on Phase 2 of the scheme at Smiths Field has commenced and this will see a 
new pedestrian/cycle route constructed alongside the river Owenass to connect with 
existing footpaths in Cullenwood estate. 
 
Active Travel Scheme, Station Rd, Portarlington 
Works are continuing on Station Road to develop safer road infrastructure and provide 
segregated off-road cycle tracks. Junction tightening, traffic calming, additional 
pedestrian crossings and front of school treatments will also be provided as part of the 
scheme. 
 
Safe Routes to School Scheme – St. Paul’s NS, 
Mountmellick 
Construction has commenced on this scheme with footpath resurfacing, new school 
zone and pencil bollards to be delivered. 
 
Bus Stop Enhancement Programme 
Laois County Council will continue to receive funding from the National Transport 
Authority in 2026 under the Bus stop Enhancement Programme.  Under the 
programme, Transport For Ireland bus stops will be upgraded to a consistent standard 
with a range of deliverables including: bus stop pole, kassel kerbing, hardstanding, bus 
cage line marking, seating or bus shelter. 
 
Bolt E-bike Hire, Portlaoise 
Bolt have been providing e-bikes for hire in Portlaoise for 18 months.  
The success of the scheme has continued throughout 2025 and the figures to the end 
of December showed that 28,000 trips have been taken in 2025 by e-bike.

• 
The new speed limits will come into effect on the dates specified by the local

Signs to be installed showing the new speed limits

30km/h speed limit to be applied to all urban centres , residential roads &

- pedestrian zones/share space zones apply 20km/h, 50km/h for Nat, Reg,
